words.example: 部署の名前を確認します。
受付で名前を伝えます。
担当の人を確認します。
この説明はわかりやすいです。
この電話は使いにくいです。

lessons.title: First day at the office
lessons.description: Introduce yourself as an intern, handle an internal call and read office instructions without confusing humble and honorific actors.
lessons.canDo: Identify the right office contact and introduce myself with appropriate modest language

grammar.title: Modest language for your own side
grammar.formation: 言う → 申す; 行く/来る → 参る; する → いたす; いる → おる. Asking/visiting a respected person: 伺う; viewing a respected person's material: 拝見する.
grammar.explanation: Use modest forms for yourself or your own side. 申す・参る・いたす・おる can make speech formal to the listener without implying that every action is directed towards them. 伺う and 拝見する lower your action in relation to a respected person or their material. Do not call a visitor's action humble on their behalf. おります is common formal 'am/is here'; unit 7's いらっしゃいます raises the other actor.
grammar.translation: I've come for the internship training (modest).

examples.ja: {資料|しりょう}を{拝見|はいけん}します。
{会議室|かいぎしつ}におります。

grammar.mistake: Use your own name + と申します. 先生がおります lowers the teacher rather than respecting them; use 先生はいらっしゃいます when respect is intended.

grammar.title: Put a question inside a sentence; name something
grammar.formation: Question word + plain clause + か + main verb. Yes/no plain clause + かどうか. Noun + という + noun. Before embedded か, noun/な-adjective present affirmative normally omits だ.
grammar.explanation: どの会議室を使うか確認します means checking which meeting room is used. There is one main statement, not two independent questions. 会議があるかどうか asks whether there is a meeting. ～という introduces a name or label: 青葉システムという会社. These constructions do not confirm the embedded proposition; someone can check whether a meeting exists without saying it does.
grammar.example: どの会議室を使うか確認します。
grammar.translation: I'll check which meeting room we will use.

examples.ja: {担当|たんとう}が{誰|だれ}か{確認|かくにん}します。
examples.en: I'll check who is in charge.

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}があるかどうか{聞|き}きます。
examples.en: I'll ask whether there is a meeting.

examples.ja: {青葉|あおば}システムという{会社|かいしゃ}です。
examples.en: It is a company called Aoba Systems (fictional course company).

grammar.mistake: An embedded question does not need a question mark after か. Use 誰か here, not 誰だか in the formal pattern practised in this unit. という labels a name, not an ability or permission.

grammar.title: Easy to do, hard to do, without doing
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem + やすい / にくい, conjugated as い-adjectives. Verb negative ない-form + で + following action.
grammar.explanation: 読みやすい describes something as easy to read; 使いにくい describes difficulty of use. These forms concern ease rather than your permission to do the action. ～ないで describes doing an action without another: 教科書を見ないで答えます. Distinguish this from ～なくてもいい, which removes an obligation, and from ～ないでください, a request not to do something.
grammar.example: 名前を確認しないで、電話をかけないでください。
grammar.translation: Please don't make the call without checking the name.

examples.ja: この{資料|しりょう}は{読|よ}みやすいです。
examples.en: These materials are easy to read.

examples.ja: この{電話|でんわ}は{使|つか}いにくいです。
examples.en: This phone is difficult to use.

examples.ja: {教科書|きょうかしょ}を{見|み}ないで、{答|こた}えます。
examples.en: I'll answer without looking at the textbook.

grammar.mistake: Use 読みやすい, not 読むやすい. ～ないで is not ～なくてもいい: 'without doing' and 'needn't do' describe different things.

dialogues.title: Meeting Mori-san
dialogues.scene: You start internship training at the fictional Aoba Systems company. Mori is your senior colleague and explains the first meeting.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: おはようございます。バオと{申|もう}します。{実習|じっしゅう}に{参|まい}りました。
lines.romaji: Ohayō gozaimasu. Bao to mōshimasu. Jisshū ni mairimashita.
lines.meaning: Good morning. My name is Bao. I've come for the internship training.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: {森|もり}です。よろしくお{願|ねが}いします。ここは{青葉|あおば}システムという{会社|かいしゃ}です。
lines.romaji: Mori desu. Yoroshiku onegai shimasu. Koko wa Aoba Shisutemu to iu kaisha desu.
lines.meaning: I'm Mori. Nice to work with you. This is a company called Aoba Systems.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: よろしくお{願|ねが}いします。どの{会議室|かいぎしつ}を{使|つか}うか、{確認|かくにん}してもいいですか。
lines.romaji: Yoroshiku onegai shimasu. Dono kaigishitsu o tsukau ka, kakunin shite mo ii desu ka.
lines.meaning: Nice to work with you. May I check which meeting room we will use?

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: {十時|じゅうじ}に{会議室|かいぎしつ}Aです。この{資料|しりょう}をご{覧|らん}ください。
lines.romaji: Jūji ni kaigishitsu ē desu. Kono shiryō o goran kudasai.
lines.meaning: Meeting room A at ten. Please look at these materials.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {拝見|はいけん}します。わかりやすいですね。{名前|なまえ}も{書|か}きます。
lines.romaji: Haiken shimasu. Wakariyasui desu ne. Namae mo kakimasu.
lines.meaning: I'll look at them. They're easy to understand. I'll write my name too.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: {電話|でんわ}の{前|まえ}に、{担当|たんとう}が{誰|だれ}か{確認|かくにん}してください。
lines.romaji: Denwa no mae ni, tantō ga dare ka kakunin shite kudasai.
lines.meaning: Before a phone call, check who is responsible.

dialogues.title: An internal call about the documents
dialogues.scene: You practise an internal call with Mori. You need the document contact, not a booking or a meal invitation.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: {内線|ないせん}{二十番|にじゅうばん}です。ご{用件|ようけん}を{伺|うかが}います。
lines.romaji: Naisen nijūban desu. Goyōken o ukagaimasu.
lines.meaning: This is extension twenty. May I ask what you need?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {実習|じっしゅう}のバオです。{資料|しりょう}の{担当|たんとう}がどなたか、{確認|かくにん}したいです。
lines.romaji: Jisshū no Bao desu. Shiryō no tantō ga donata ka, kakunin shitai desu.
lines.meaning: This is Bao, the intern. I'd like to check who is in charge of the materials.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: {森|もり}です。{私|わたし}に{聞|き}いてください。
lines.romaji: Mori desu. Watashi ni kiite kudasai.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {先|さき}ほど、{十時|じゅうじ}に{会議室|かいぎしつ}Aとおっしゃいましたね。{鍵|かぎ}は{受付|うけつけ}で{受|う}け{取|と}りますか。
lines.romaji: Sakihodo, jūji ni kaigishitsu ē to osshaimashita ne. Kagi wa uketsuke de uketorimasu ka.
lines.meaning: You said earlier, meeting room A at ten. Do I collect the key at reception?

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: はい。{受付|うけつけ}で{名前|なまえ}を{伝|つた}えてから、{受|う}け{取|と}ってください。
lines.romaji: Hai. Uketsuke de namae o tsutaete kara, uketotte kudasai.
lines.meaning: Yes. Tell reception your name, then collect it.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: わかりました。{名前|なまえ}を{確認|かくにん}してから、{部屋|へや}に{入|はい}ります。
lines.romaji: Wakarimashita. Namae o kakunin shite kara, heya ni hairimasu.
lines.meaning: Understood. I'll check the name, then enter the room.

readings.title: Internship orientation sheet
paragraphs: {青葉|あおば}システムへようこそ。
{実習|じっしゅう}の{担当|たんとう}は{森|もり}です。
{質問|しつもん}がある{時|とき}は、{内線|ないせん}{二十番|にじゅうばん}で{連絡|れんらく}してください。
{初日|しょにち}の{会議|かいぎ}は{十時|じゅうじ}から、{会議室|かいぎしつ}Aです。
{鍵|かぎ}は{受付|うけつけ}にあります。
{受付|うけつけ}で{名前|なまえ}を{伝|つた}えてから、{鍵|かぎ}を{受|う}け{取|と}ってください。
{名前|なまえ}を{確認|かくにん}しないで、{鍵|かぎ}を{持|も}っていかないでください。
{資料|しりょう}に{自分|じぶん}の{連絡先|れんらくさき}を{書|か}いてください。

glosses.kana: れんらくしてください

glosses.text: 持っていかないでください
glosses.kana: もっていかないでください

watch.prompt: Optionally save five lines from a workplace scene in your own media. Identify whose action is modest or respectful and whether an embedded question actually has an answer. Fictional businesses are not a model for every company's etiquette.

exercises.prompt: Why has Bao come to the company?
exercises.explain: 実習に参りました states the purpose.

exercises.prompt: Where and when is the meeting?
exercises.explain: 十時に会議室Aです gives both details.

exercises.prompt: Who is in charge of the materials?
exercises.explain: Mori identifies himself and says 私に聞いてください.

exercises.prompt: What comes before collecting the key at reception?
exercises.explain: 名前を伝えてから establishes the order.

exercises.context: Introduce your own name modestly to an office colleague.
exercises.explain: Your own name takes と申します; おっしゃいます raises someone else's saying.

exercises.context: You don't yet know whether there is a meeting. Say you will check this yes/no issue.
exercises.line: {会議|かいぎ}がある＿＿、{確認|かくにん}します。
exercises.explain: かどうか embeds a yes/no question without asserting its answer.

exercises.context: Say the materials are easy to read.
exercises.line: この{資料|しりょう}は{読|よ}み＿＿です。
exercises.explain: 読み + やすい expresses ease, while にくい would express difficulty.

exercises.context: Describe answering without looking at the textbook; this is not permission to omit it.
exercises.line: {教科書|きょうかしょ}を{見|み}＿＿、{答|こた}えます。
exercises.explain: 見ないで describes the absence of looking while answering.

exercises.context: You are describing your own arrival for training to a senior office colleague. Use modest language for your action.
exercises.prompt: Which is the requested modest introduction?
options: {実習|じっしゅう}にいらっしゃいました。
{実習|じっしゅう}を{召|め}し{上|あ}がりました。
{実習|じっしゅう}に{参|まい}りました。
exercises.explain: 参りました is modest came; いらっしゃいました raises the actor, and 召し上がる is eat/drink.

exercises.line: ご{用件|ようけん}を{伺|うかが}います。
exercises.context: You need to identify the person responsible for the materials. State that purpose.
options: {資料|しりょう}の{担当|たんとう}を{確認|かくにん}したいです。
{夕食|ゆうしょく}をごちそうさまでした。
{鍵|かぎ}を{落|お}としてしまいました。
exercises.explain: The first reply states the materials-contact request; the others give unrelated business.

exercises.line: この{資料|しりょう}をご{覧|らん}ください。
exercises.context: Agree to look at the colleague's materials, using the humble viewing expression for your own action.
options: {私|わたし}がご{覧|らん}になります。
{私|わたし}がおっしゃいます。
exercises.explain: 拝見します lowers your viewing action; ご覧になる raises someone else's viewing.

exercises.meaning: I'll check who is in charge.
exercises.explain: 誰か embeds the question; 確認します is the main statement.

exercises.prompt: Which contact is specified for questions?
exercises.explain: The guide names Mori as the training contact and 内線二十番 for questions.

exercises.prompt: Where does the first-day meeting begin at ten?
exercises.explain: 初日の会議は十時から、会議室Aです gives the first-day meeting.

exercises.prompt: What must come before taking the key?
options: Giving and checking the name at reception
exercises.explain: The guide says to tell reception your name first, and not take the key without checking it.

exercises.prompt: What information should be written on the materials?
exercises.explain: 自分の連絡先を points to your contact details, not the meeting contact's.
